t:
(a) In General.—There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs for the Construction, Major Projects, account—

        (1) for fiscal years 2001 and 2002, a total of $87,800,000 for the projects authorized in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of section 231(a); 
        (2) for fiscal year 2001, an additional amount of $23,600,000 for the project authorized in paragraph (4) of that section; and 
        (3) for fiscal year 2002, an additional amount of $14,500,000 for the project authorized in section 401(1) of the Veterans Millennium Health Care and Benefits Act (Public Law 106–117; 113 Stat. 1572).  
    (b) Limitation.—The projects authorized in section 231(a) may only be carried out using—

        (1) funds appropriated for fiscal year 2001 or fiscal year 2002 (or, in the case of the project authorized in section 231(a)(4), for fiscal year 2001) pursuant to the authorization of appropriations in subsection (a); 
        (2) funds appropriated for Construction, Major Projects, for a fiscal year before fiscal year 2001 that remain available for obligation; and 
        (3) funds appropriated for Construction, Major Projects, for fiscal year 2001 or fiscal year 2002 (or, in the case of the project authorized in section 231(a)(4), for fiscal year 2001) for a category of activity not specific to a project.  
    (c) Revision to Prior Limitation.—Notwithstanding the limitation in section 403(b) of the Veterans Millennium Health Care and Benefits Act (Public Law 106–117; 113 Stat. 1573), the project referred to in subsection (a)(3) may be carried out using—

        (1) funds appropriated for fiscal year 2002 pursuant to the authorization of appropriations in subsection (a)(3); 
        (2) funds appropriated for Construction, Major Projects, for fiscal year 2001 that remain available for obligation; and 
        (3) funds appropriated for Construction, Major Projects, for fiscal year 2001 or fiscal year 2002 for a category of activity not specific to a project.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for VA major construction projects and limits which funds may be used to carry them out. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs for the Construction, Major Projects, account

qwen_block.w: This section is purely an authorization of appropriations and sets limitations on how those funds may be used. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and the funding sources, all of which are internal to the government.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs for the Construction, Major Projects, account

opus.w: This section only authorizes appropriations for VA major construction projects and limits which funds may be used for them. It has no consultation, public comment, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision. Mentions of authorized projects and cross-references to other laws are funding mechanics, not a participation process.
opus.b: This section is about money only. It authorizes funding for VA construction projects and limits which funds can be used. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The one possible trap is that it refers to "authorized" projects and to other laws, but none of that involves outside participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes and limits the use of federal funds for construction projects. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The only actors involved are federal officials (Secretary of Veterans Affairs) and Congress, which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text references "projects authorized in... section 231(a)", and those projects might involve public input, this section implies participation. However, this section itself is purely an appropriations clause, limiting how funds can be spent. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or advisory process involving non-federal parties. The actors mentioned are the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (federal) and Congress (federal). There is no mention of states, tribes, the public, or outside experts being consulted or involved in the decision-making process described in this specific text.
